This excursion explores Inca heritage around Cusco. Over 4–5 hours, you will see the massive walls of Sacsayhuaman, the Qenqo sanctuary, Puka Pukara and Tambomachay — archaeological sites illustrating different aspects of Inca engineering and religious traditions.

Sacsayhuaman is the first major stop. The original description presents it as a ceremonial fortress, built with enormous stone blocks fitted precisely together and offering panoramic views over the Cusco area.

The route then continues to Qenqo. In the original itinerary, this site is described as an ancient Temple of the Puma, with labyrinthine passages and a stone altar associated with rituals.

The next stops are Puka Pukara and Tambomachay. Puka Pukara stands on elevated ground and is described in the original material as a fortification connected with control of the routes. Tambomachay is included as another example of Inca architecture. After lunch, there is free time to explore Cusco independently.

Mendoza was founded in the 16th century, when the area belonged to Chile. In the 19th century, a powerful earthquake almost completely destroyed the old city. Little of its original buildings survived, including the ruins of the Church of Saint Francis.

Today, Mendoza remains remarkably green despite its location in an arid region. Around 80,000 trees have been planted in the city, along with an extensive network of canals. During the tour, you will see Plaza España and Plaza Independencia, with their cafés and restaurants, San Martín Park and the Hill of Glory, with its monument to José de San Martín. The hill offers panoramic views of the city and the surrounding dry landscape.

The tour takes place in the historic center, a UNESCO World Heritage Site.

You will see colonial facades and traditional Portuguese tiles.

During the tour, you will visit Gonçalves Dias Square, Palácio dos Leões, the Church of São José de Ribamar, the Central Market and the Reviver district, with its well-preserved historic houses.

The route also offers panoramic views of the city.

The tour introduces local cuisine as well. One example is arroz de cuxá, a regional rice dish made with seasonings and local ingredients.

## Full-Day Tour of Lake Titicaca

Lake Titicaca, a sparkling jewel of the Andes, is a place where history, culture and nature come together in remarkable harmony. Its deep-blue waters, nestled high in the mountains, are said to reflect the sky, creating a tranquil, almost otherworldly atmosphere. As the world's highest navigable lake, Lake Titicaca is steeped in ancient legends and the living traditions of the Indigenous peoples who call its shores and islands home. Every sunrise and sunset over the lake is a spectacle, bathing the horizon in golden hues that dance across its vast, calm surface.

Our first stop will be the floating reed islands of the Uros. The friendly residents of these man-made islands will welcome us warmly and demonstrate their techniques for building reed boats and islands.

Our boat will then continue to Taquile Island, where local people still preserve their ancestral traditions and wear bright traditional clothing. This is a wonderful opportunity to explore the island and enjoy magnificent lake views. A typical lunch will be offered at a local restaurant. Toward sunset, our boat will return to the pier in Puno.

## Taquile Island

Taquile Island, a peaceful haven in the middle of Lake Titicaca, seems to transport visitors to another time. The islanders proudly preserve their ancient customs, reflected in their colorful handwoven textiles and traditional clothing. Terraced hillsides offer sweeping views of the deep-blue lake and the distant peaks of the Andes, creating a landscape that feels both immense and intimate. Life on Taquile moves at a gentle pace, making it an ideal place to experience nature and the rich cultural heritage of the local people.
